name: xTool D1 Pro 5W
tagline: 5W engraving-first module on xTool's open-frame D1 Pro rail
tldr: The 5W D1 Pro module is xTool's engraving-first head on the open-frame D1 rail : fine marks on wood, leather, and coated metal with occasional thin cuts. Swap to 10W–40W modules later on the same chassis.

priceRange.note: 5W optical module : verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cannot: Clear acrylic cutting (diode light passes through)

pros: Lowest D1 Pro entry : large 430 × 390 mm bed at engraving-first wattage
Fine spot size for photo fills, leather gifts, and coated metal marks
Swappable head : upgrade to 10W–40W modules on the same rail
xTool Creative Space onboarding plus LightBurn for production
Ideal if cutting thick stock is rare and mark quality matters most
cons: This module targets thin cuts (about 3 mm basswood class) : not thick production plywood
Higher modules in this line (10W, 20W or 40W) add cut speed and depth
Not the SKU for a shop cutting 3 mm+ stock all day
Open frame: kids, pets, and smoke are not contained
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 5W module on xTool D1 Pro. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Optimize for engraving: lower DPI on photos, higher scan speed on line art after test burns. Air assist still helps clarity. Compare benchmark times on the next module before assuming you need more power.
mainObjective: Detailed engraving on organics and coated metal : occasional thin cuts only

images.alt: xTool D1 Pro 5W laser engraver : xTool

moduleSystem.headline: Swappable diode modules on D1 Pro frame
moduleSystem.description: xTool D1 Pro uses plug-in diode modules (5W–40W depending on era and listing). Buy the module power you need : same rail and software as other D1 Pro heads.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 5W D1 Pro module is the right buy when your revenue is mostly marks on wood, leather, and slate, not plywood production. You get xTool's large bed and clear upgrade path without paying for cut watts you will not use weekly.
editorialDepth.limitations: Shops that quote box cutting or thick basswood daily should open the 10W, 20W, or 40W profiles before checkout. Open-frame means glasses and ventilation are non-negotiable. Cast acrylic and bare metal without spray stay out of scope.
